brief.headline: Memory rally extends into Q3; HBM supply sold out through 2027, CoWoS constraints easing by year-end
brief.summary: <cite index="12-6,12-7">DDR4 8Gb spot prices hit $24 in July, up 14.3% MoM, while general-purpose NAND (128Gb MLC) rose 4.3% to $30.1.</cite> <cite index="11-1">TrendForce projects Q3 DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ and NAND Flash +10-15% QoQ</cite>, decelerating from Q2's record 58-63% and 70-75% jumps but still reflecting structural AI-driven supply diversion. <cite index="8-3,8-13">Top three memory makers have pre-sold full HBM output for 2026, with Micron guiding 68% gross margins in Q2 2026.</cite> <cite index="20-2,20-6">Hyperscalers collectively committed $660-690B in 2026 capex, nearly doubling 2025 levels, with 75% directed at AI infrastructure.</cite> <cite index="29-5,29-7">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026 as monthly capacity reaches 120-140K wafers.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025, followed by Samsung at 22% and Micron at 21%.</cite> <cite index="52-1,52-13">Samsung finally passed Nvidia's 12-layer HBM3E qualification in September 2025 and reached volume shipments in October 2025, with 2026 supply reportedly sold out.</cite> However, Samsung remains third supplier after 18-month delay vs. SK Hynix's first-mover advantage on H100/H200. <cite index="53-1,53-3">Samsung will start mass producing HBM4 for Nvidia in February 2026</cite>, but SK Hynix retains pole position on next-gen roadmap. Relative value favors SK Hynix on pricing power and Nvidia allocation depth; Samsung optionality hinges on HBM4 yield execution and share gain vs. entrenched HBM3E incumbents. Post-July 31 rebound (+30% SKH, +27% Samsung) resets technicals but fundamentals still tilt Hynix.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="11-9,11-10">Demand for AI inference and hyperscale data centers keeps DRAM/NAND supply constrained as manufacturers shift capacity toward higher-margin server products, leaving less capacity for consumer memory.</cite> <cite index="13-9,13-10">TrendForce cites declining willingness to pay on buyer side—memory prices already so high that PC, smartphone, and consumer manufacturers cannot accept every further increase.</cite> <cite index="8-11">Bank of America forecasts global DRAM revenue +51% in 2026 and NAND +45%, with ASPs climbing >30%.</cite> Pricing momentum moderating from Q1-Q2 vertical spike but still double-digit QoQ through Q3. Structural shortage narrative intact through 2027 per supply discipline and HBM cannibalization of commodity fab capacity.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-6">UBS notes HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1B Gb.</cite> <cite index="5-3">Channel checks indicate SK Hynix will secure ~50% market share in 2026.</cite> <cite index="5-4">Nvidia negotiations with Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron ongoing; possible pricing pushback as Samsung inches closer to HBM3E qualification</cite>—though that risk has crystallized with Samsung now shipping. <cite index="8-9">SK Hynix is the only supplier able to deliver both HBM3E and next-generation HBM4 at scale.</cite> <cite index="1-5">Micron's HBM3E 36GB 12-high integrated into AMD Instinct MI350 Series.</cite> <cite index="5-7">Hynix expects only minimal-to-modest HBM3E price downtick for 2026 vs. 2025.</cite> Key watch: HBM4 qualification timing (Samsung Feb 2026 start vs. SK Hynix/Micron readiness) and Nvidia allocation split for Rubin platform in H2.

news_pulse.headline: DDR4 and NAND spot prices hit record highs in July on AI demand
news_pulse.implication: DDR4 8Gb at $24 (+14.3% MoM) and NAND 128Gb MLC at $30.1 (+4.3% MoM) confirm pricing power persists in commodity segments despite moderation vs. Q1-Q2 vertical moves. Reinforces margin expansion thesis for Samsung/SK Hynix conventional DRAM/NAND mix.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix surge ~27-30% on record single-day gains (July 31)
news_pulse.implication: Violent rebound following July selloff; catalyzed by Amazon/MSFT earnings affirming hyperscaler AI capex commitment. <cite index="40-8">SK Group Chairman Chey disclosed share purchases, bolstering confidence.</cite> Technical reset but valuation stretched post-rally; watch for foreign follow-through beyond short-cover.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance raised to $660-690B, up 36-81% YoY
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="19-5,19-6">Big Five (Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle) will spend >$600B in 2026, with ~75% ($450B) targeting AI infrastructure.</cite> <cite index="25-8">Allianz Research: divergence between AI capex and revenue growth at ~46%, exceeding 2001 telecom cycle's 32%.</cite> Demand visibility remains strong but ROI scrutiny rising—monitor any guidance cuts in next earnings cycle.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap to narrow from 20% to 10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="29-2,29-7">TSMC monthly CoWoS capacity could reach 120-140K wafers in 2026.</cite> Easing packaging bottleneck should enable higher GPU/accelerator shipments in H2, supporting incremental HBM demand. Positive read-through for SK Hynix/Samsung HBM unit shipment expectations.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung begins HBM4 mass production for Nvidia in February 2026
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="53-1,53-3">Samsung completed Nvidia HBM4 qualification, with production scheduled February 2026.</cite> Closes gap vs. SK Hynix on next-gen roadmap but timing still lags Hynix's first-mover position. Share gain opportunity in Rubin cycle if yield/performance competitive; pricing risk if Samsung discounts to build share.

news_pulse.headline: Memory makers have pre-sold full 2026 HBM output; Micron at 68% GM in Q2
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="8-3,8-13">Top three memory makers allocated full HBM output for 2026; Micron guiding 68% gross margin in Q2 2026.</cite> Pre-sold capacity through 2027 per most analysts; pricing discipline should hold absent macro demand shock. HBM gross margins 2-3x conventional DRAM—mix shift accretive for Samsung/SK Hynix.

news_pulse.headline: UBS: SK Hynix to hold ~50% HBM market share in 2026, HBM bits +35% YoY
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="5-1,5-6">TSMC call signals AI demand ahead of forecasts; HBM bit shipments to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1B Gb.</cite> <cite index="5-3">Channel checks indicate SK Hynix ~50% share.</cite> Reinforces Hynix as primary beneficiary of HBM upcycle; Samsung/Micron share gains contingent on yield execution and Nvidia allocation.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q3 DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="11-1">Q3 DRAM contract prices to rise 13-18% QoQ, NAND Flash 10-15%</cite>—deceleration from Q2's 58-63% / 70-75% but still robust. <cite index="11-9,11-12">Server demand healthy through 2027 as improving CPU availability supports AI server deployments.</cite> Consumer pushback capping upside but enterprise/AI pricing intact.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI 200 futures likely elevated post-July 31 rally; implied vol should compress after record 14% KOSPI single-day jump. ADR premium/discount for SSNLF and HXSCL worth monitoring vs. KRX close—arb opportunities if US session lags Korean momentum. Options skew likely flattened; any renewed volatility favors short-dated straddles around earnings (Samsung typically late-July, SK Hynix late-October for Q2/Q3). Watch USD/KRW—strengthening dollar headwind to ADR translation, though memory pricing in USD mitigates operational FX exposure.
watch_for_next_3h: Any Samsung or SK Hynix disclosures on HBM4 qualification timing or customer announcements (Nvidia Rubin, AMD MI400, Broadcom/Google custom)
Hyperscaler earnings call commentary on AI capex pacing—particularly Amazon, Microsoft, Meta follow-up after July 30-31 results drove rally
TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot price updates for early-August DRAM/NAND—confirm July momentum sustained or fading
TSMC CoWoS capacity utilization data or customer commentary on packaging lead times for H2 2026 GPU/accelerator shipments
